anchors.statement: The plan-anchoring skill and its harness-specific agents must conform to claude-code-skills-agents-guidelines.md except where a locked anchor records a user-approved override.
anchors.quote: these guidelines are my expected baseline.
anchors.scope: edits the skill, an agent definition, an agent registry, an invocation runner, or plugin orchestration
anchors.deterministic_check: Run the Phase A compliance validator against the guideline-derived rules and the documented override list.

pass: The Phase A change follows every applicable guideline rule and records the Agent-tool override in the locked anchors.
fail: The change ignores the guideline because the current implementation already works.

anchors.statement: Claude plan-anchor workflows must invoke subagents with the Agent tool and contain no instruction to invoke the superseded Task tool.
anchors.quote: yes, the Task tool has been superceeded w/ Agent tool
anchors.scope: edits Claude delegation instructions, invocation examples, agent manifests, or orchestration tests
anchors.deterministic_check: Repository validation finds Agent-tool invocation and no active instruction that invokes the Task tool.

pass: Claude invokes anchor-plan-review through the Agent tool.
fail: Claude invokes anchor-plan-review through the Task tool.

anchors.statement: The orchestration boundary must resolve each agent's registry entry, canonical path, version, model, and SHA-256 once and pass an immutable runtime descriptor to the agent.
anchors.quote: why does every agent need to do this?
anchors.scope: adds or changes agent resolution, registry validation, runtime attestation, or an agent preflight step
anchors.deterministic_check: Runner tests prove one resolution per invocation and agent definitions contain no install-path fallback search.

pass: The runner resolves the registered agent path, version, model, and hash once before launching it.
fail: Each agent searches several installation paths and validates its own version before starting.

anchors.statement: Each agent invocation must supply exactly one fenced JSON params object whose fields match the agent's documented Inputs contract.
anchors.quote: is the agent getting passed fenced json input?
anchors.scope: edits any Claude or Codex agent invocation example, runner payload, or agent Inputs contract
anchors.deterministic_check: A contract test parses exactly one fenced JSON input object for every registered agent and rejects missing required fields.

pass: The invocation contains one fenced JSON params object matching the registered agent input schema.
fail: The invocation describes script, tracker, and item values as unstructured prose.

anchors.statement: Plan-anchor must read no application-specific environment variable except TYPESAFE_API_KEY.
anchors.quote: My preference would be no environment variables are used outside of typesafe api key
anchors.scope: adds or changes configuration, command-line flags, defaults, installation instructions, or environment reads
anchors.deterministic_check: Static validation finds no plan-anchor-owned environment read other than TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

pass: The script reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY and receives model, endpoint, threshold, and limits through CLI arguments or defaults.
fail: Users must export PLAN_ANCHOR_ALLOW_REMOTE_JUDGE and PLAN_ANCHOR_JEV_MODEL before running a gate.

anchors.statement: --dry-run and fixture-answer execution must make zero network calls, proven by transport-spy unit tests.
anchors.quote: yes, --dry-run is an arg that does the same thing and can be used in unit tests
anchors.scope: changes dry-run, fixture-answer, transport, rubric, tuning, or gate execution
anchors.deterministic_check: Unit tests fail if any transport is called during --dry-run or fixture-answer execution.

pass: The dry-run and fixture-answer tests use a transport spy that observes zero requests.
fail: Dry-run validates the request and then sends it to Jev.

anchors.statement: The skill must support both bd and br through tracker-neutral operations after selecting one installed tracker at the orchestration boundary.
anchors.quote: how large of a change would it be to make this skill work w/ bd and br ?
anchors.scope: reads, creates, updates, lists children of, or comments on tracker issues
anchors.deterministic_check: Contract tests run the same normalized show, children, create, update, and comment cases against bd and br fixtures.

pass: The tracker layer selects br and normalizes show, children, create, update, and comment results.
fail: The planning agent calls bd children directly and fails in a br repository.

anchors.statement: Agent params must omit interpolated shell command strings, carrying a tracker descriptor and operation data instead.
anchors.quote: so the bd/br commands would be passed in the fenced json?
anchors.scope: edits tracker selection, agent params, runner payloads, or tracker command construction
anchors.deterministic_check: Input-schema tests reject command-string fields and adapter tests construct argv from validated operation data.

pass: Params identify tracker br and issue pa-123 while the trusted adapter constructs the argv list.
fail: Params contain the interpolated command string br show pa-123 | jq .

anchors.statement: Harness-specific agent definitions are separate under .claude/agents and .codex/agents, declaring Sonnet/Opus for Claude and Luna/Sol for Codex.
anchors.quote: I think we should have separate agents for codex and claude (in .codex/.claude folders so agent class sonnet/luna are specified per harness).
anchors.scope: adds or changes an agent definition, registry entry, plugin manifest, or model assignment
anchors.deterministic_check: Version-sync validation proves registry parity and the expected Sonnet/Opus and Luna/Sol role assignments.

pass: Claude definitions live under .claude/agents with Sonnet and Opus roles while Codex definitions live under .codex/agents with Luna and Sol roles.
fail: Both harnesses load one shared agent file with an unspecified model.

anchors.statement: Question tuning must run in an evaluator independent from the planner, freeze an oracle from approved intent and anchors, and ignore whether the current plan passes.
anchors.quote: tuning should be done w/ an agent independent from the planner.
anchors.scope: changes question-tuning prompts, oracle construction, fixtures, override acceptance, or tuner model selection
anchors.deterministic_check: Tuner contract tests prove the oracle is fixed before Jev answers and current plan verdicts are absent from tuning inputs.

pass: The tuner freezes its oracle from approved intent and fixtures before the first Jev answer and never receives the current plan verdict.
fail: The planner rewrites questions until the currently failing bead passes.

anchors.statement: Documentation must identify Jev as required for the normal workflow and describe dry-run and fixture modes as development and CI aids.
anchors.quote: fix README and make sure documents are consistent (this skill requires jev)
anchors.scope: edits README, SKILL.md, installation guidance, examples, or marketplace descriptions
anchors.deterministic_check: Documentation consistency validation finds the required-workflow statement and no claim that offline modes replace Jev.

pass: The README states that Jev is required for normal capture, tuning, and gate execution and labels offline modes as development aids.
fail: The README presents dry-run as a complete replacement for Jev.

anchors.statement: All script outputs and persisted run data must redact the TypeSafe API key and bearer-token forms before emission.
anchors.quote: the code-redaction change is a real issue flint fixed.
anchors.scope: changes transport errors, structured output, logging, reports, audit records, or run-file persistence
anchors.deterministic_check: Secret-canary tests scan stdout, stderr, errors, reports, audits, and run files for raw credential and authorization-header variants.

pass: A transport failure returns a redacted credential marker and no run artifact contains the supplied secret.
fail: A structured error echoes the supplied API key in its suggested action.

anchors.statement: Examples must use repository-valid paths, current command syntax, and JSON shapes emitted by supported tracker and harness versions.
anchors.quote: p3 - update examples to be realistic
anchors.scope: adds or changes README examples, reference snippets, fixtures, sample anchors, or agent invocation examples
anchors.deterministic_check: Example tests execute commands in a fixture repository and validate documented JSON against current schemas.

pass: The br example uses docs/plans/phase-a, current flags, and the documented br JSON envelope.
fail: The example uses an invented path, removed flag, and JSON shape no supported tracker emits.

anchors.statement: The plan-anchor plugin must not define or invoke the sc-lint agents arch-qa or req-qa.
anchors.quote: where did arch-qa and req-qa come from?  these are agents on sc-lint, not part of this skill
anchors.scope: edits plan-anchor agent files, registries, manifests, skill delegation, or examples
anchors.deterministic_check: Repository search finds no arch-qa or req-qa reference under the plan-anchor plugin.

pass: The plan-anchor registries list only anchor-plan-review, anchor-sprint-review, and anchor-question-tune.
fail: The plan-anchor skill delegates requirement review to the sc-lint req-qa agent.
